title: keyed record search over a 0x30-byte-stride table, 0x141b331f0
notes: Read from the body: prefilter on rec[0x10] and rec[0x18] (and rec[0x20] when r9b is non-zero), then a sticky partial-match flag - set by any record with rec[8] != 0 and rec[0] == 0 - decides whether a record whose rec[8] equals key[8] is a candidate. The last candidate wins; an exact match (rec[0] == key[0]) returns immediately.
The return is eax, zero-extended into rax by `mov eax, ebx`, so it compares as a u64 and -1 reads 0xffffffff.
ucov: no calls and no globals - the body is self-contained, which is why it was the first pick from dev/queue.py.
acknowledgedGaps: What the records and the key describe is not read: the unit pins the arithmetic, not the meaning of the fields.

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: `if count <= 0 { return -1 }` widened to `count < 0`: at count == 0 the loop runs zero times and `best` stays -1, so the early exit and the loop exit produce the same value. Equivalent for every input, not just this corpus.
